correctness.rationale: For every positive integer k, a part of size n_i has signed neighbor count Delta-delta_i, so a permanently mixed part is tied in both phases; all moving homogeneous parts flip. The fixed-state equations rule out a mixed-plus-homogeneous fixed point and give just two unanimous states plus equal half-occupancy words if all four sizes are even. In any primitive two-cycle with a mixed part, averaging the two phases excludes fixed homogeneous parts, and equal weights of opposite flipping groups forces 3k+4k=7k, leaving the 2k shore arbitrary and frozen. The sixteen all-homogeneous shore signs have only the two cycles already corresponding to extreme frozen words. A symmetric threshold bilinear energy with adjacency plus I/2 excludes eventual periods >2. Independent weighted part-occupancy enumeration k=1..4 reproduced fixed and two-orbit counts (2,4),(28828802,16),(2,64),(33394325524560002,256); this finite evidence corroborates, not proves, all k. The proof covers k>=1 with individual vertex labels and incumbent tie-retention, not transient basin sizes.
